title: EMA Flags Schizophrenia Drug Paliperidone Shortage in EU States Over Pharmathen Manufacturing Issues
summary: Bengaluru: The European Medicines Agency on Thursday disclosed a shortage of an injectable medicine used to treat schizophrenia in some member EU states due to issues at contract manufacturer...

contentHtml:
Bengaluru: The European Medicines Agency on Thursday disclosed a shortage of an injectable medicine used to treat schizophrenia in some member EU states due to issues at contract manufacturer Pharmathen International.

Paliperidone palmitate, the drug in ‌short ⁠supply, is ⁠used as a treatment in adults with schizophrenia ​whose condition has been stabilized with antipsychotic drugs like paliperidone ​or risperidone.

The shortage affects medicines marketed by Advanz Pharma, Adamed Pharma, Alter, Belupo, Biogaran, EGIS Pharmaceuticals, Elpen, ​G.L. Pharma and Innovis ⁠Pharma, the ‌EMA said.

The shortage could also ​affect other ​long-acting injectable medicines containing paliperidone palmitate ⁠in additional countries, the regulator added.

The regulator said ​manufacturing problems at the Greek contract ​drug manufacturer Pharmathen had caused a shortage, adding the shortage was not linked to product quality defect or safety concern.

Pharmathen did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for ‌comment or details on the issue or how many facilities were affected.

The EMA ​said there ​was no ⁠known end date for the shortage, and advised healthcare professionals to consider alternative medicines where needed.

The agency ​said some of its departments are closely monitoring the supply situation and engaging with the companies marketing the drug to mitigate the impact of the supply shortage.
